sessions.title: Design and Build a Gamified Onboarding Agent with M365, Copilot and Power Platform Workshop
sessions.description:
Most organisations already have some form of onboarding content, and some have tried chatbots or simple agents to help new employees. But many of these experiences are flat, hard to navigate and quickly ignored.

In this full-day workshop, a game designer, a Power Platform / CodeApps expert and a Microsoft 365 & Copilot expert guide you through the complete process of designing and prototyping a Gamified Onboarding Agent that could actually live in each company.

sessions.title: Agent Academy Live! Workshop
sessions.description:
In this workshop, you will learn how to build successful agents using Microsoft Copilot Studio. Loosely based on the Microsoft Agent Academy content, we will guide you through the fundamentals of agent development and progress to advanced techniques including multi-agent orchestration, content moderation, and enterprise integrations.

Whether you're new to AI agents or looking to enhance your skills, this hands-on workshop will equip you with practical knowledge to design, build, and deploy intelligent agents that solve real-world business challenges. Through a combination of guided instruction, live demonstrations, and hands-on labs, you'll experience the full agent development lifecycle, from your first conversation to production-ready solutions.

sessions.title: Building an AI Superhighway: Hands-On Enterprise AI Gateway with Azure API Management Workshop
sessions.description:
Your organisation has gone all-in on AI. Teams are deploying models through Microsoft Foundry, someone's using AWS Bedrock for Claude, another team's calling Google Gemini directly. Developers are exposing internal APIs as MCP servers for agents. A platform team is piloting agent-to-agent communication using the A2A protocol. The innovation is exciting - but costs are unpredictable, security postures vary by team, and when leadership asks "how much are we spending on AI?", you're piecing together answers from five different dashboards. Agents are calling tools and other agents with no central governance. The experimentation phase was fun, but it's becoming unsustainable.

In this hands-on workshop, you'll build a working AI gateway using Azure API Management that routes every AI call - models, MCP tools, A2A agents - through a single control plane, regardless of where they're hosted. You'll deploy infrastructure, write policies, break things, and fix them.

sessions.title: Zero Trust, Zero Compromise: Operationalising Microsoft Security in 2026 Workshop
sessions.description:
Zero Trust isn’t a slide deck anymore. It’s the baseline.

In 2026, identity is the control plane. AI-driven phishing, token replay, MFA fatigue, cloud lateral movement and ransomware-as-a-service have made perimeter thinking obsolete. The question is no longer “Should we adopt Zero Trust?” — it’s “Is our Microsoft estate actually operating that way?”

This workshop is built for architects, security leads, and senior engineers who want to move beyond theory and design a Zero Trust architecture that works in the real world.

No marketing. No vague maturity models.

Just practical implementation across the Microsoft security stack.

We’ll break down how to operationalise Zero Trust across:

Identity (Entra ID, Conditional Access, identity governance)
Endpoint (Intune posture, compliance signals, device risk)
Threat detection (Defender XDR correlation across identity, endpoint and cloud)
Data protection (Purview as an active enforcement layer — not just compliance)
Executive alignment (building a roadmap leadership will actually fund)

sessions.title: New Speakers Workshop
sessions.description:
Do you attend events and look at those on stage wondering how to get there, or are you interested in speaking but don’t know how to get started or whether if you even have something valuable to share?

We firmly believe that everyone has a story - everyone has a different perspective, different experiences, different learnings and can contribute their own story in a way that will be valuable to someone out there.

This workshop is for you if you are just getting started on your speaker journey and looking to polish your skills, or not yet a speaker and looking to get into speaking at events, but don’t know how to get started.

We will break down the mystery of speaking at tech events by providing clear, practical steps that make the process accessible to everyone. Our workshop is designed to demystify what often seems like a black box, offering actionable guidance and real-world advice to help you confidently begin your speaker journey.

sessions.title: Scottish Summit 2026 Keynote
Building with Heart in the Age of AI
sessions.description: AI makes producing probably-working software easier than ever. But the further we step from the code, the less control we have. DevOps shows us guardrails matter when delivering value at scale. So how do we move fast but avoid sleepwalking into brittle systems that only appear correct? When is "good enough" enough, and where do creativity and taste come in?

sessions.title: AI Innovation. Data Foundation.
sessions.description: In this session, we'll explore how Azure NetApp Files provides the high-performance storage foundation for both SQL Server and AI workloads in Azure. Learn how organisations can unlock the value of their existing SQL data to power analytics, intelligent applications, and generative AI solutions. We'll cover real-world architectures, performance optimisation techniques, and practical approaches to building AI-ready data platforms that accelerate innovation while maintaining enterprise-grade performance and reliability.

sessions.title: Designing Intelligent Tool-Driven Agents
sessions.description:
Modern Copilot Studio agents can do far more than answer questions—they can reason, act, collaborate with humans, and make controlled decisions.
In this session, we will build an agent step-by-step to demonstrate how Copilot Studio’s expanding toolset enables powerful, safe, and flexible automation scenarios.

We’ll walk through how to use each tool individually and then combine them into a coordinated workflow:

AI Prompt to generate dynamic content and chain reasoning

AI Approval to introduce governed decision points

Human-in-the-Loop to collect user input or expert confirmation

Adaptive output tools to shape responses

Other Copilot Studio tools that enable integrations, data actions, and workflow branching

By the end of the session, you’ll understand how to orchestrate these capabilities inside a single agent, enabling it to make automated decisions, request human oversight where needed, and produce high-quality, context-aware outputs.

Attendees will leave with a clear blueprint for constructing robust Copilot Studio agents that blend AI automation with responsible controls—ideal for enterprise use cases such as approvals, content generation, customer support, data processing, and more.

sessions.title: Seeking Your Approval: Mastering Approvals in Microsoft 365
sessions.description:
With all of the emails piling up in your inbox and Teams chats pinging left and right, it can be easy to miss that quick, "Hey, does this look good?" question from a colleague. Using Microsoft Approvals can be a great way to have a concrete, separate place to collect those approvals. In this session, you will learn:
*How to build a variety of types of approvals in Power Automate
*How to view those approvals in Microsoft Teams
*Use cases for building processes around approvals

This session will enable audience members to build their own approval solutions, whether simple and straight-forward or more complex and layered.

sessions.title: Closing the Loop: How a Small Security Team Refined an Enterprise-grade DLP solution
sessions.description:
Managing an enterprise-grade DLP solution tends to mean getting buried under an endless mountain of audit logs, scrambling to apply exclusions and refinements to controls based on sporadic incident tickets, end user complaints and assorted dumpster fires. For example, when users are constantly uploading files to an ever-changing array of cloud services, keeping your Endpoint DLP authorized domain list accurate to exclude approved services from file upload controls can rapidly overwhelm a small security team.
 
This session introduces a practical, automated approach to solving this issue, based on a solution adopted successfully by real security teams in the field. We will explore how to set up a continuous refinement loop that does the heavy lifting for you, leveraging smart Endpoint DLP audit rules, the Graph API runHuntingQuery endpoint and Azure Logic Apps to bring actionable intelligence directly to security responsibles, right in the flow of everyday work in Teams.
 
In this session, you will learn how to:
- Set up dedicated Endpoint DLP rules and other pre-requisites to silently monitor file uploads against your baseline of approved domains.
- Use Logic Apps to automatically query the Graph API runHuntingQuery endpoint and gather audit events of unauthorized file uploads.
- Filter weekly audit findings into a clean, concise and actionable report, supported by a more comprehensive CSV dataset.
- Deliver these insights straight into a Teams channel so admins can effortlessly review and update allowed domains in minutes.

The proven pattern explained and demonstrated in this session is one you can apply to countless other security and governance scenarios going forward, helping manage sprawl and helping keep your organization secure with less friction.
 
This session is well-suited for security responsibles and admins, IT Pros as well as anyone interested in effectively operationalizing security solution refinement with limited resources.

sessions.title: Azure Foundry - Lets build some agents
sessions.description:
Let’s build some agents! 

In this session, we’ll dive into Azure AI Foundry and create agents live, showing how they can think, act, and work together to solve real problems. From orchestrators to specialists, you’ll see how easy it is to bring ideas to life and wire them into your business. 

Expect demos, a few surprises, and practical takeaways you can use to start your own agent journey the moment you leave the room.

One thing I will also cover is when to use Foundry over Copilot Studio, I expect some discussions on this from the room!

sessions.title: 🚀 Copilot Cowork in Action: What It Is, How to Get It & What You Can Do With It
sessions.description:
A lot of people have heard of Cowork, but there is still a gap between hearing about it and actually knowing how to use it. How do you get access? What does it look like in practice? And what can it realistically help you with day to day?

This session is here to close that gap. Join us for a practical, demo-driven showcase where we walk through Cowork from the ground up. You will see it in action across real scenarios: managing your inbox, staying on top of meetings, collaborating with your team, and getting things done faster inside Microsoft 365. We will not just tell you what is possible, we will show you the reality.

What makes this session a little different is that you will hear from both the Microsoft side and the partner side. That means you get a balanced view: the vision and direction behind Cowork, alongside real-world experience of adopting and using it in practice. Two perspectives, one session.

By the end, you will know exactly how to get access, what to expect when you first open it, and which use cases are worth exploring straight away. We will highlight the features that make the biggest difference in everyday work, demonstrate what those look like live, and give you a clear starting point to take back with you.

This session is for anyone who works in Microsoft 365 regularly, whether you are in IT, a power user, or just someone looking to get more out of the tools you already have. No deep technical background required. If you are curious about Cowork and want to leave with something concrete, this is the session for you.

sessions.title: From Overwhelmed to In Control: An Essentialist Approach to Running a Power Platform CoE
sessions.description:
Running a Power Platform Centre of Enablement can feel like trying to build a plane while you’re mid-flight. New features arrive weekly, demand grows faster than capacity and governance expectations never slow down. No wonder so many Centre of Enablement leads feel overwhelmed before they even start. 

This session introduces an Essentialist approach to governing and managing Power Platform, inspired by the principles in Greg McKeown’s 'Essentialism'. Instead of trying to do everything - and burning out in the process - you’ll learn how to identify what actually matters, make intentional trade-offs, and build a sustainable, focused CoE practice that works whether you’re a team of ten or a team of one.

Drawing on years of experience supporting customers and running our own Power Platform CoEs, we will share practical, field-tested strategies for cutting through the noise, creating an environment where makers and stakeholders get what they need - maximising value without driving everyone to burnout.

Key takeaways include:
1. How to apply Essentialism’s trade-off mindset to governance decisions so you stop chasing everything and start prioritising what truly moves the needle.
2. Simple automated routines to eliminate clutter in your environment and processes, helping you maintain oversight without drowning in dashboards, reports, or manual reviews.
3. How even small organisations can run an effective CoE without needing an enterprise-size budget or team.

You’ll leave with a clear sense of direction, renewed confidence, and a set of repeatable routines to help you stay in control - even when the platform seems to be evolving at light speed.

sessions.title: Deep dive into debugging & monitoring SPFx production solutions
sessions.description:
"Hello IT, I have a problem with this app... Here's a screenshot."

And here begins all the trouble. What exactly happened? How do I repro the issue? In this session, we'll go through various front-end debugging approaches, such as using debug manifest file or source map, and how can we monitor user activity with Azure App Insights.

If you're a developer and have already faced production issues, this session will interest you for sure!



Key takeaways:

- SPFx bundling: a reminder about the process
- Production debug: difference between existing solutions and choose what's the best depending on your case
- Relevant logs: how to create powerful logging system which will interact with App Insights

sessions.title: Automated Testing for Fabric: What Works and What Doesn’t
sessions.description:
Microsoft Fabric promises an end-to-end analytics platform, but when it comes to testing, the reality is far less clear-cut.

In this session, I’ll share what testing Fabric actually looked like on a large government transformation programme, where data pipelines, Power BI, CI/CD, and automation all collided under real delivery pressure. This isn’t a “best practice” talk—it’s an honest account of what worked, what broke, and what we had to rethink along the way.

We’ll start by setting the context: what Fabric changes about testing, where traditional approaches fall down, and the new risks that appear when you move from APIs and UIs to analytics, pipelines, and reports. From there, I’ll walk through concrete examples from real code, pipelines, and Power BI artefacts—covering data validation, flaky automation, CI/CD integration, and how we decided what not to automate.

The session closes with a worked example and a clear set of takeaways that teams can apply immediately.

You’ll leave with:

Practical approaches to testing Fabric pipelines and Power BI outputs without chasing false confidence

Ways to define meaningful test oracles for data quality and analytics

Examples of automation patterns that helped—and anti-patterns that slowed teams down

Ideas for structuring CI/CD feedback in fast-moving data platforms

Session structure (flexible: 40–60 minutes)

Core talk (40 minutes):

10 mins – Context: Fabric, analytics testing, and real-world constraints

20 mins – Lessons learned: pipelines, visuals, automation, and CI/CD

10 mins – Worked example and concrete takeaways

sessions.title: Creating Classifiers from Scratch to Identify Sensitive Data with Microsoft Purview
sessions.description:
Microsoft Purview offers a wide range of data security solutions, including Information Protection to protect data, Data Loss Prevention to prevent data leaks, Data Lifecycle Management to control the data lifecycle, and Insider Risk Management to detect and respond to insider risks.

The first step for many organizations is to classify their sensitive data. One approach is letting users take charge and classify the data themselves. But if we want to make the most of the platform, we need Microsoft Purview to understand what sensitive data looks like in our environment.

In this session, we are going to create classifiers that enable Microsoft Purview to identify, classify, and protect sensitive data. Join me as we explore Sensitive Information Types, Custom SITs, Fingerprint SITs, Exact Data Match SITs, Trainable Classifiers, and more.

By the end of this session, you will have the skills to create classifiers in Microsoft Purview from scratch and the knowledge to know when to use which one. This will help you make the most of the platform for your organization.

sessions.title: Azure Virtual Network Manager: Herding Networks the Easy Way
sessions.description:
If you’re running workloads in Azure, you already know the world of Virtual Networks, subnets, IP ranges, and all the moving parts that come with cloud networking. 

But have you met Azure Virtual Network Manager: the service that finally brings centralized governance and consistency to your network landscape?

Instead of managing each Virtual Network separately, Azure Virtual Network Manager gives you a single control plane to define, deploy, and enforce network configurations across your entire environment. Even better, it introduces long‑awaited capabilities like built‑in IP Address Management that previously required third‑party tools or custom solutions.

In this session, we’ll walk through how to configure Azure Virtual Network Manager from the ground up, explore its strengths, and shine a light on its limitations so you know exactly what to expect before adopting it.

When you head home after the event, your backpack will be filled with:
	- Guidelines for setting up Azure Virtual Network Manager
	- A clear understanding of its key features and how to use them effectively
	- Real-world scenarios where AVNM is not the right choice
	- All demo code so you can deploy everything in your own environment

Join me for a practical, honest, and demo-heavy deep dive into one of Azure’s most powerful new networking tools.

sessions.title: Multiversal Mental Health & Accessibility
sessions.description:
Caught in the Mental Health Multiverse? 
Seeking Wisdom from the Forbidden Fount of "Questions that you've always wanted to ask but never dared to"? 
Looking for Top Tech Tips across the Microsoft Galaxy of Ginormousness ? 
Or just wanting to stop off at the Hyperspace Hangout and seek out new connections and new communities?

Join a panel of people who live with Mental Health, Neurodiversity, and Disability - but love tech, love life, and love just having fun and sharing all they can.

Firstly we will be popping in to the Nebula of Knowledge where we will traverse Crucial Copilot Commands, to Intergalactic M365 and Windows Wisdom, and stopping by the Portal of Power Platform Perception.  All giving out invaluable ideas and tips for levelling up your daily accessible life - either as a user or as a developer.

Then the Oracles of Openness will be taking all questions from the floor (in a filtered way to avoid any mishaps). Ask those questions that you've always wondered but were afraid to ask. Get particular insights and ideas. Hear from the years of experience and challenge.

You'll leave with a toolbox of tips and ideas, and a mind full of knowledge and insight - as well as a network of like-minded souls to accompany you on your next mission into unknown space.

sessions.title: The Architect’s AI Playbook: Patterns, Pitfalls, and Proven Prompts to tame technical debt
sessions.description:
AI is rapidly changing how software is designed, built, and governed—but for architects, the real value of Copilot is not simply writing code faster. The bigger opportunity lies in accelerating troubleshooting, strengthening quality gates, producing living documentation, tightening security, and systematically reducing technical debt across teams.
In this session, we’ll walk through a practical Architect’s Playbook for using GitHub Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot in real-world architecture and delivery workflows. Starting from common architectural pain points, we’ll explore proven patterns for applying Copilot in the IDE and pull request lifecycle, as well as across Teams, Word, and PowerPoint using organizational context. Live examples will demonstrate how architects can use Copilot to reason about unfamiliar codebases, review changes more effectively, document decisions as they evolve, and support governance without slowing teams down.
We’ll also take an honest look at where AI assistants fall short. You’ll see concrete examples of hallucinations, insecure or misleading suggestions, and compliance blind spots—and learn how to recognize and mitigate these risks through guardrails, prompt structure, and workflow design. The goal is not blind trust in AI, but safe and intentional operationalization at scale.
By the end of this session, attendees will leave with reusable prompt structures tailored for architectural work, reference workflows they can apply immediately with their teams, and a clearer mental model for when Copilot accelerates outcomes—and when it requires human judgment.

sessions.title: Intelligent Structured Document Generation in SharePoint
sessions.description:
The Problem
Many organisations rely on standard documents such as contracts, letters, reports, and statements of work, yet the way these documents are created is often manual, inconsistent, and difficult to govern. Small variations, copy‑and‑paste edits, and formatting drift can quickly lead to rework, errors, and a lack of uniformity.

What you’ll cover
Intelligent structured document generation in SharePoint brings together document templates, Forms, and AI to create repeatable, well‑governed documents based on existing Word files. Instead of manually editing documents or relying on fragile automations, content is generated consistently from approved templates, with AI helping to identify and manage fields and placeholders.
The session explores how the new SharePoint structured document generation capability works in practice and where it fits within broader SharePoint and Copilot scenarios. It covers how existing Word documents can be converted into reusable templates, how Forms act as the entry point for document creation, and how different roles are involved in designing, governing, and consuming generated documents.
Real‑world scenarios are used throughout to show where this approach delivers clear value, as well as common mistakes to avoid.

Key takeaways
Attendees will leave with a clear understanding of when structured document generation is the right approach, how it differs from traditional document automation, and how to apply it sensibly in their own SharePoint environment.

Tech & tooling
SharePoint, Microsoft Word, Microsoft Forms, Copilot

sessions.title: Privileged Access is Broken (Even When You Think It Isn’t)
sessions.description:
Most organisations believe their privileged access is secure.

Multi-Factor Authentication is enabled. Conditional Access policies are in place. Privileged Identity Management (PIM) is configured. On paper, everything looks right.

In practice, privileged access remains one of the most common paths to compromise.

This session explores why.

Rather than focusing on individual controls, this session examines how privileged access is actually used in real-world environments, and why environments that appear secure frequently fail under operational pressure. Drawing on familiar patterns from on-premises administration through to modern cloud environments, it highlights how common behaviours such as convenience, speed, and “just getting it done” introduce risk, even when the correct controls are in place.

The session then introduces a structured, practical approach to improving privileged access, focusing on how identity, access policies, device trust, and operational practices must work together as a cohesive system rather than isolated features. Particular attention is given to isolation as a critical but frequently overlooked control in modern environments.

Attendees will leave with a clear understanding of where typical implementations fall short, and how to take practical steps to improve their own environments using the tools they already have.

This session will reference Microsoft Entra ID, Conditional Access, and Privileged Identity Management (PIM), and is aimed at Level 200 attendees who are familiar with these controls and want to understand how to apply them effectively in real-world scenarios.

sessions.title: Event-Driven DevOps: Automating Azure with Event Grid System Topics
sessions.description:
Modern DevOps on Azure isn’t just about pipelines, it’s about making your platform reactive. With Event Grid system topics, you can automatically respond to changes in your Azure environment, triggering workflows the moment resources are created, updated, or deleted.

In this session, we’ll cover:
- How system topics work and how they fit into DevOps workflows
- Connecting Event Grid to various automation and orchestration tools
- Different practical use cases for event-driven automation
- A live demo where a resource change triggers a deployment-related automation

After this session, you’ll walk away with practical techniques to make your Azure platform more event-driven, reducing manual steps, closing feedback loops, and bringing DevOps automation to the next level.

sessions.title: Agent 365: If It’s Not Built with Copilot Studio...Does It Still Work?
sessions.description:
Microsoft is slowly but surely positioning itself as the vendor of choice for managing the ever-growing AI agent ecosystem. When governance, security and oversight are critical, the capabilities in tools such as Microsoft Agent 365 provide the toolsets to understand an organisation's entire agentic ecosystem. But how well does this actually play ball if we decide not to use Copilot Studio or Microsoft Foundry as our agent development platform? Is it really as easy as they say to bring in any agent to Agent 365 and to reap the same touted benefits?

In this session, we're going to go "off-script" and work through how we can bring a totally awesome, but completely non-Microsoft, agent into the Agent 365 control plane. Attendees will gain an understanding of how Agent 365 can support this objective, the limitations involved and see a live demo on how to onboard a non-Microsoft-hosted agent into the tool. The end result? A full appreciation of the Microsoft Agent 365 capabilities and the importance of having good governance and oversight tools to drive your journey into the world of agentic AI.

And if we can't get this ultra-new-and-shiny platform feature working? Then it's simple. We'll cheat 😛

sessions.title: Agents for Everyone: The Reality of Rolling Out Copilot Studio at Public Sector Scale
sessions.description:
What happens when you open up AI agent creation to 30,000 employees in a UK government agency?
 
In this session, Keith (Power Platform & AI Architect, Capgemini) and Cliodhna (Power Platform Service Manager, Defra) share the real story of rolling out Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365 Agent Builder across a large public sector organisation.
 
The goal was simple: empower people across the organisation to build their own AI agents to support their daily work. The reality was more complex.
 
We’ll talk openly about the journey so far, including the decisions, challenges, governance questions, adoption hurdles, technical considerations, and cultural shifts involved in enabling AI agent creation at scale. We’ll also share what has worked well, where expectations needed to be managed, and the achievements that have made the effort worthwhile.
 
This is not a polished "everything went perfectly" case study. It is an honest conversation between supplier and customer about what it really takes to introduce AI agents safely, responsibly, and practically in a large government organisation.

sessions.title: Building a Responsible AI Centre of Excellence That Actually Delivers
sessions.description:
AI adoption is accelerating across every organisation, but very few have the structures in place to scale it safely, ethically and sustainably.

In this session, we move beyond theory and explore how to design and operationalise a Responsible AI framework through a practical AI Centre of Excellence model.

This session will cover:

• What Responsible AI really means in a Microsoft ecosystem
• How to establish an AI Centre of Excellence that enables innovation without creating bottlenecks
• Balancing compliance, governance and commercial pressure
• Practical guardrails for Copilot, Azure AI Foundry and AI agents
• Managing risk, drift and misuse in production AI systems
• Embedding monitoring and observability using Azure Monitor and Purview
• Defining roles, ownership and decision rights across IT, security and the business

Attendees will leave with:

• A blueprint for launching an AI CoE
• A practical governance operating model
• Real-world patterns for scaling AI responsibly
• A clear view of how to align Responsible AI principles with measurable business value

This session is ideal for architects, technical leaders, security professionals and decision-makers who want to move from experimentation to enterprise-scale AI with confidence.

sessions.title: Think like a hacker in five steps
sessions.description:
Everybody knows that you should not plug in a random USB stick, right? With some simple tricks your users might be convinced otherwise. Hacks, data breaches, ransomware. Protecting your company can be hard if you don’t know what you’re looking for. Security starts with just that and what better way to figure out than by attempting to hack yourself or your co-workers. 

You might have guessed it already; this talk is about hacking in any way possible. We will explore how hackers operate and I’ll show you some of the tools. Is your application really safe, and what to look for in those applications.

Finally, we will touch upon the most painful “people” hacks, what happens when you’re a good talker? Can you convince users to do exactly those things they are instructed to never do. Can your helpdesk employees be persuaded to reset your password over the phone? Let someone enter your building because they “forgot” their badge. 

Now that we are talking about badges, what about physical security. Have you ever seen someone clone a hotel keycard? One randomly selected audience member will get the chance to try just that with some cheap electronics

sessions.title: Productivity Hack Battle: Top 10 tips for busy (and easily distracted) tech professionals
sessions.description:
Are you drowning in tasks, messages, and meetings? It's time to take back control of your workday.

Easy? Just point your task list and calendar at your favorite Copilot/AI agent and it'll take care of it, right? Right?!

Hmm, maybe not.

Instead of another boring set of slides or wild vendor promises (ahem, Microsoft), our two presenters face off in... (big announcer voice):

THE PRODUCTIVITY HACK BATTLE!

Each presenter shares 5 killer productivity hacks, tools, and agents that help them work smarter, not harder. Not just the "what," but the "how."

From time management tricks to automation secrets to focus techniques that actually work when your brain won't cooperate, you'll get a rapid-fire tour of 10 proven tips. Some are tested traditional methods. Some are AI and agents done right. All of them are built for how real brains actually work, not how productivity gurus wish they did.

But this isn't just another talk: YOU get to be the judge.

After the hacks are revealed, the audience votes live on which ones are the most game-changing.

You'll walk away with new tools and habits to boost your efficiency without burning out, and without needing to force yourself into a system that was never built for you.

Don't miss this chance to level up your productivity and find out which hack wins the ultimate showdown.

sessions.title: Would You Trust This Agent?
sessions.description:
Copilot and agent experiences can create real value, but only when they fit the way people actually work. In operational services, users do not just need speed. They need confidence, context, and a clear sense of when to trust the AI, when to check it, and when a human should take over.

This session focuses on one practical question: what makes an AI-assisted workflow feel trustworthy enough to use? Using realistic service scenarios, it will show where human-in-the-loop matters, why happy-path demos are not enough, and how poor workflow design can make Copilot or agents feel risky instead of useful. It will cover a handful of common use cases such as summarisation, triage support, knowledge retrieval, and next-best-action prompts, and show how to assess whether they genuinely reduce effort or simply add another layer of uncertainty.

Attendees will leave with a lightweight trust checklist they can apply before building. The goal is to help teams design Copilot and agent experiences that support operational work in a clearer, safer, and more adoptable way.

Key takeaways
Attendees will learn how to identify stronger and weaker Copilot or agent use cases, where human review matters most, how to design for exceptions rather than just happy paths, and how to make AI-assisted workflows easier for users to understand and adopt.

sessions.title: From Zero to Fully Local AI: Building a Working LLM App with Foundry Local
sessions.description:
Everyone is talking about sovereignty — in cloud infrastructure, data centers, and now increasingly in AI. But what does AI sovereignty really mean in practice? Can Microsoft Foundry Local help us build a sovereign AI solution, or is it simply an on-premises AI setup that ensures data does not leave our environment?

In this session, we will explore what Foundry Local is, where it fits into the Microsoft AI ecosystem, and what role it can play in scenarios where data control, privacy, compliance, and local execution matter. We will look at the requirements, the installation process, and the key components needed to get started.

The goal of this session is to move beyond buzzwords and provide a practical first look at running AI locally with Microsoft Foundry Local. Attendees will leave with a better understanding of what is possible today, what limitations to expect, and how to take the first steps toward building local AI-powered solutions.

sessions.title: Hidden Disabilities – Courage, Awareness & the Challenge of Speaking Up in IT
sessions.description:
IT culture celebrates resilience. "Always on." Always performing. Always available. But what happens when the person behind the keyboard is fighting something invisible?

In 2024, I was diagnosed with lymphoma, incurable, and now a permanent part of my life. That diagnosis forced a choice: hide it until I couldn't, or speak openly. I chose openness. And it changed everything about how I show up at work.
This session explores the intersection of hidden disabilities and IT culture,  a space where vulnerability rarely fits into sprint cycles or incident queues, and where the pressure to appear "operational" can silence struggles that deserve to be heard.

We'll examine:
Why do IT professionals, especially men, find it so hard to speak up about health challenges
The bias that equates illness with unreliability in technical roles
The emotional cost of masking a disability while solving everyone else's problems
What leaders, teams, and individuals can do to create genuinely inclusive workplaces

You'll leave with personal insights, practical guidance, and a new perspective on what strength really looks like in tech.

Because strength and vulnerability aren't opposites. They're allies.

sessions.title: Teaching Copilot to Speak Your Language: The Future of Smarter Meetings
sessions.description:
The use of Copilot to boost workplace productivity continues to grow. Most Microsoft apps and services now have an AI assistant embedded to support users with more on the way. Among Microsoft’s collaboration tools, Microsoft Teams, the hub for teamwork, is steadily evolving with AI-powered features and agents designed to make chats and meetings more seamless.

These AI capabilities enhance the meeting experience both during and after the session. Participants can focus and engage more attentively while Copilot takes notes automatically. While many appreciate the convenience of AI-generated meeting summaries, a common challenge continues to persists. It has been observed that the AI notes often contain misspellings or awkward phrasing, especially when unique organisational acronyms are involved.

Having stated the challenge, the good news is that a solution is now available, thanks to the latest updates from the M365 Roadmap. The introduction of a custom dictionary in Copilot allows organisations to tailor AI-generated notes with the correct terms and phrasing, improving clarity and readability.

In this session, I’ll cover:

- The process structure of capturing team-specific organisational acronyms

- Requirements and steps for implementing a custom dictionary in Copilot for Teams meeting

- Real-world use cases demonstrating the custom dictionary in action

By the end of this session, organization administrators will be better equipped to help team members and stakeholders to fully benefit from AI-generated notes during and after Microsoft Teams meetings.

sessions.title: Bouncing back from failure
sessions.description:
In 2015, I was called into a meeting and told that I was being let go. I was married, two children and a third on the way. 
In 2003, I hit DROP ALL TABLES on a production database with no backups.
In 2000, I failed my university exams and was hit with the decision of paying for another year of university or giving up.
In 2022, I was turned down by twice as many conferences as accepted me.
In 2026, I managed to kick everyone out of my first ever keynote by mixing End Event with Leave Meeting.

Why have I put it in that order? Not because of the timeline but because the lower in the list, the better I became at bouncing back. Through these failures, I have learnt new things, changed my ways of thinking, changed the way I do things and learnt about resilience.

Do I find it easy when I fail? No.
Do I put I smile on my face quicker now? Yes.
Have I learnt how to learn and plot my way forward fast? Yes

In this session, I will build on my own experience of failure and the ways I learnt to bounce back. I will bring some science to the story and the academic stories to support my own experience. From these, I will share some meaningful suggestions that you can take to build your own ways to bounce back too.

Plus, at the end, I will happily sit with everyone to share their own stories and their own ways of building resilience and ways to move forward.

sessions.title: Agent Inception: Using AI to Build AI for Microsoft 365
sessions.description:
Using an AI to build an AI agent. It sounds like a circular logic puzzle, but it is actually the most efficient way to build for Microsoft 365 Copilot today. 

In this demo-heavy session, we explore the "Inception Workflow": combining GitHub Copilot with the new Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit Skills.

We will transition from zero to a fully deployed, high-quality declarative agent in under 20 minutes without manually authoring a single JSON manifest or instruction file.

You will learn how "Skills" provide coding agents with the deep schema knowledge and guardrails needed to scaffold projects, integrate API plugins and craft sophisticated system instructions. Stop hand-coding your manifests and start shipping with the power of the AI.

Key Takeaways
- The Power of Skills: Understand how curated knowledge modules eliminate "hallucinations" in agent manifest creation.
- Master the Prompt-Scaffold-Iterate workflow to collapse development time from hours to minutes.
- Instruction Engineering: See how to use AI to write robust, safe and professional personality instructions for your agents.
- Zero-Friction Deployment: Watch a live transformation from a natural language prompt to a deployed agent running in Copilot.

sessions.title: Agent Builder vs Copilot Studio: Choosing the Right Tool for AI Agents
sessions.description:
There are multiple ways to build AI agents on Microsoft’s platform, but most organisations begin with the low-code options: Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio. The challenge is knowing which one to use, and when.

In this session, we'll take you through a practical, hands-on comparison of Agent Builder and Copilot Studio. Using live demos and real-world examples, we’ll show what each tool is designed for, where their strengths lie, and where they start to fall short as requirements become more complex.

We’ll also cover how to improve your prompts and design better agents, how to deploy agents across different channels, and what your options are when you need to go beyond the low-code experience using tools like Microsoft Foundry.

Whether you are new to AI agents or looking to enhance your skills, you’ll leave the session with a clear way to choose between Agent Builder and Copilot Studio, and a better understanding of how to design agents that scale as your needs grow.

sessions.title: 🧠 Model Context Protocol vs. Connectors: Rethinking Integration in the Power Platform 💡
sessions.description:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) quickly became the thing everybody talks about who is doing AI in the moment and its adoption rate across different tech providers is rapid. Microsoft has embraced it as well and is combining it with an old friend of ours: (Custom) Connectors.

In this session, we will break down the differences between Model Context Protocol (MCP) and traditional connectors in the Power Platform. Attendees will learn how each works, where they fit best, and how they compare. The session includes practical demos showing how to get started with MCP and how it can work alongside connectors—not replace them. It’s aimed at solution architects, developers, and IT leaders looking to modernize how they build integrations.

Do not miss this session if you want to get your AI solutions to the next level which will be increasingly connected to other system and working with your data. We will discuss if connectors together with MCP will get us to the true agentification which was promised.

sessions.title: Power Pages with BYOC: Lessons learned from customer implementation
sessions.description:
“Bring Your Own Code” in Power Pages sounds like a dream: build whatever you want, host it directly on the platform, and move fast. In practice, it’s a powerful option, but one that changes more than you might expect.

In this session, I’ll walk through a real customer project where standard Power Pages wasn’t enough, and we made a conscious decision to go all‑in on hosting a custom Single‑Page Application inside Power Pages.

I’ll focus on the actual solution we built, the architectural decisions behind it, and the trade‑offs we had to make along the way. I’ll cover the journey from the first “can we even do this?” discussions to a live deployment, including the constraints, surprises, and mistakes we learned from.

We’ll dive into how authentication and Dataverse integration work with a custom front end, what BYOC means for security and ALM in a real project, and how team roles and development practices shift when pro‑code meets the Power Platform ecosystem.

This is an honest session aimed at architects and developers who want to understand when BYOC makes sense.

Key takeaways:

- A concrete view of how a custom SPA communicates with Dataverse and surrounding systems when hosted via Power Pages. A real live architecture, not theory.
- Practical insights into how development workflows, team responsibilities, and delivery models change when moving from standard Power Pages to BYOC.
- Hard‑earned lessons on security, performance, integrations, and ALM, based on what actually worked and what didn’t in a customer project.

sessions.title: Trusted Data for Trusted AI
sessions.description: Join us to explore why data quality is the foundation of successful AI. Learn how accurate, validated and enriched data helps organisations improve AI outcomes, reduce risk, and make more confident decisions. We'll show how Data8's data quality, verification and enrichment solutions help create trusted, AI-ready data that delivers real business value.

sessions.title: The Human Hack: Rebooting Consulting Culture
sessions.description:
This isn’t about tools, templates, frameworks, or even just the latest AI technologies it’s about people and mindset. In this honest and practical session, we explore how as consultants and delivery leads, we can rediscover and develop better consulting cultures in a world obsessed with tools and delivery speed.  

Expect a candid conversation as two seasoned leaders in the Microsoft consulting community are interviewed by a fellow highly experienced leader. The session will be filled with, stories, audience Q&A, and actionable advice you can put straight into action back on your projects and in your teams.  Bring your questions and get involved. 

You’ll leave with new ways to:  

- Sharpen your critical thinking skills and learn how to ask the right questions to get to the true root of a problem. 

- Build strong, trusting relationships with clients by encouraging open communication, curiosity, and teamwork. 

- Make sure your work delivers clear, measurable business value by considering its impact on people, processes, and technology. 

If you’ve ever felt like your work was technically perfect but somehow missed the mark, this session will show you why and how to fix it. Take away new ways to think, lead, and consult that make your engagements more rewarding, your impact more visible, and your career genuinely fulfilling.   

AI is driving a significant shift in the consulting landscape, encouraging a heightened focus on tools, templates, and frameworks risking the loss of the human experience and mindset. Don’t let yourself drift into transactional delivery. Join us to reclaim the mission, rebuild the mindset, and become the kind of consultant the industry desperately needs.

sessions.title: Replacing VPN with Entra Private Access: The Bits That Worked and the Bits That Bit Back
sessions.description:
The VPN is the bit of infrastructure everyone wants gone but nobody fancies replacing. Entra Private Access is meant to fix that. In places it does. In others it makes you realise how much your tired old VPN was quietly carrying.
This session is what a production migration actually looks like once the slide deck is shut. Connector group design that survives a single failure. Conditional Access patterns for private apps. The discovery work most rollouts underestimate, because half the apps are doing things over protocols nobody documented.
Live demo of Per-App Access end to end, gated by Conditional Access. Then the failure modes. Legacy apps that don't behave, DNS pointing at the wrong place, licensing that turns into a small spreadsheet by accident. Plus where Private Access sits inside Global Secure Access, and the cases where the honest answer is to keep the VPN around for another six months.
Attendees leave with a deployment plan that survives contact with reality, a Conditional Access policy set worth copying, and a clearer view of what Private Access actually does well versus what's still not there.
Aimed at identity and security folk who know Entra ID and Conditional Access and are either looking at Private Access seriously or partway through a rollout that's started raising awkward questions.
Tech & tooling: Microsoft Entra Private Access, Global Secure Access, Conditional Access, Entra ID, Entra Internet Access.

sessions.title: Azure Automation Done Right: Build It Like You Mean It
sessions.description:
Most Azure Automation environments share the same problem: runbooks living directly in the portal, credentials hardcoded in plain text, and no recovery plan when something breaks. This session shows what a production-ready Azure Automation setup actually looks like, based on real environments built over years of consulting work.

We cover Source Control integration so your runbooks are version-controlled and deployable like real code. Key Vault for credentials, so nothing sensitive ever sits in a variable store. The practical difference between App Registrations and Managed Identities, and how to decide which one fits your scenario. And Hybrid Workers for organisations that still have on-premises infrastructure that Azure cannot reach on its own.

You will leave with a clear picture of what separates a working automation from one you can trust in production, and the concrete steps to close that gap.

sessions.title: AI Legislation: What You Need to Know
sessions.description:
With AI legislation slowly being introduced and varying wildly from country to country, it is not easy to identify what you need to know about it when it comes to creating, using and managing Microsoft Business Applications and Power Platform solutions. Join this session to get an overview of:
•	The AI legislation, regulations and standards as they currently stand globally (EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, AIDA, ISO/IEC)
•	What current legislation applies to Microsoft solutions
•	Existing Microsoft tools you can use now to address legislation
•	How to future proof your solutions to remain compliant
Being aware of the legislation requirements now will allow you to plan and have the right governance and controls in your tenant – and even beat the deadlines!

sessions.title: Stop Sending Journeys. Start Conversations. Building AI-Driven Customer Dialogues in Dynamics 365
sessions.description:
Most “customer journeys” are still one-way broadcasts dressed up as personalization. We send emails, wait for clicks, and call it engagement.
With Conversational Journeys, Dynamics 365 Customer Insights finally enables something different: real, adaptive customer dialogue.

In this session, I take you behind the scenes of building intelligent, conversation-driven journeys that react to customer intent, behavior, and context in real time.

You’ll learn how to:
* Design conversational journeys
* Integrate AI agents
* Connect Contact Center interactions

Focused demos and real life experience, this session gives architects and consultants practical guidance for turning “AI-powered engagement” into potentially scalable, reliable solutions.
Leave with the mindset, patterns, and technical foundations to move from campaigns to conversations.

sessions.title: Spark joy in Microsoft 365: Marie Kondo your data
sessions.description:
Join us for an engaging, life-changing, and sometimes “on no do I need to delete things” session where we apply the principles of Marie Kondo's KonMari Method™ to declutter and organize your Microsoft 365. In this session we will guide you through a step-by-step process to tidy up your digital workspace, ensuring that every email, document, folder, site, and Team sparks joy and serves a clear purpose.

Objectives:
•	Understand the core principles of the KonMari Method™ and how they can be applied to digital spaces.
•	Learn practical techniques for assessing and organizing your content.
•	Develop a personalized plan to maintain a tidy and efficient place to store your and your team's data.

By the end of this session, you'll have a clear and actionable plan to transform your workplace into a well-organized, efficient, and joyful digital workspace. Say goodbye to clutter and hello to productivity!

sessions.title: The LinkedIn Blueprint: Building Your Brand and Network in the Microsoft Ecosystem
sessions.description:
Building a career in the Microsoft space can feel like doing great work in a crowded room where no one can hear you. Technical expertise grows, projects succeed, and knowledge deepens - yet recognition and MVP nominations don’t always follow. Many highly skilled professionals remain “Invisible Experts,” missing opportunities not because they lack ability, but because their professional presence is hidden.

In this session, you’ll discover how to use LinkedIn as a professional identity layer to showcase your expertise and build authentic connections without turning it into a second job. Through practical examples and a live profile walkthrough, we’ll bridge the gap between deep technical competence and community visibility.

Key Takeaways:

- Practical steps to make your technical skills, achievements, and project wins stand out to the Microsoft community.

- A simple framework for sharing technical insights and lessons learned without the “social media cringe.”

- Techniques for building meaningful relationships with internal teams, MVPs, and the wider community.

- Habits for maintaining a strong professional presence in just minutes each week.

Join this session and ensure you are never the “best-kept secret” in the Microsoft space again.

sessions.title: Urgent access without security compromise!
sessions.description:
Imagine this: Your Lead Architect is on holiday abroad. A major incident hits your home base, requiring their immediate intervention on a highly sensitive project. The clock is ticking. Do you compromise your security standards to let them in, or keep the door locked and risk the project?

You don't have to choose.

Join your presenters as they reveal how to solve the "Security vs. Availability" paradox. Learn how to leverage the integration of Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Purview to create a dynamic access solution that adapts to crises without lowering the drawbridge.

Key takeaways include:

- Dynamic Geo-Filtering: Configuring Conditional Access to adapt to user location without exposing the environment.
- Label-Based Logic: utilizing Sensitivity Labels as the trigger for granular access controls.
- Global Governance: Implementing Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) to secure data assets everywhere, from the corporate office to a hotel Wi-Fi.

sessions.title: More To Life Than Work
sessions.description:
Scottish Summit is built by people, and people do not leave their real lives at the door. Behind the scenes of careers, community work, speaking, organising and “doing it all”, many of us are also balancing caring responsibilities, family pressures, health challenges, and the general weight of trying to keep everything moving at once. This panel is an open and honest discussion about that reality.

Hosted by the Scottish Summit organisers, this session is a true safe space for a frank and human conversation about balancing career growth, community involvement, and caring duties while protecting your own wellbeing. We will talk about pressures, compromises, support systems, and the importance of asking for help, in a setting where people can feel heard, understood, and not judged.

sessions.title: Fantastic Fabric: From Data Chaos to Real-World Insights
sessions.description:
Modern data platforms often start in chaos. Multiple tools, disconnected processes, and growing complexity, making it harder to turn data into meaningful insights. Separate tools for ingestion, transformation, storage, and reporting makes solutions harder to manage and slows teams down, making it genuinely difficult to deliver insights efficiently.

Microsoft Fabric addresses this challenge by bringing these capabilities together into a unified platform. Built within the familiar Power BI ecosystem, it provides a consistent experience for both business users and data professionals.

In this session, we walk through a real-world approach to building an end-to-end data solution in Microsoft Fabric—from ingesting raw data, through transformation and modelling, to delivering insights. Rather than focusing on theory, the session explores practical implementation approaches and the challenges that arise when using Fabric in real scenarios.

You will see how core components such as Dataflows, Pipelines, Lakehouse, Warehouse, external tables, and Workspaces (including security roles) fit together in practice, and how to design solutions that are scalable, maintainable, and aligned with business needs.

The session also highlights common pitfalls such as inefficient data modelling, orchestration gaps, and performance issues, along with practical ways to avoid them.

In addition, it covers key topics such as migration considerations from Azure Synapse to Fabric, Direct Lake reporting, basic PySpark notebooks for data transformation, and the Medallion architecture.

From this session, you'll get a clear and practical understanding of how to build effective solutions in Microsoft Fabric, including design patterns that work, common mistakes to avoid, and techniques to improve performance and delivery.

This session is aimed at data professionals and anyone working with data who want to move beyond the basics and start building real-world solutions using Microsoft Fabric.

sessions.title: Sheep herding with Agent 365
sessions.description:
You've drunk the Kool Aid. You've built the agents. You've taught your colleagues to build agents. Now you have 7753 agents and there's only 1000 people in your company! What do you do now? Can you handle 67 agents called Policy Agent? Can you trust people to connect to the sources they should be using? What happens if someone shares their Agent Builder Agent with all 1000 people? Do you just panic and leave? Or do you let Agent 365 become your sheepdog.
 
Microsoft's answer to this is Agent 365, the "single solution" to manage your agents. Through Microsoft 365, Power Platform, Purview and more, Microsoft has brought together many different stories into a more aligned story that can help you bring control and understanding to your tenant. Pipe and shepherd's crook optional.
 
This session will outline more of the horror stories that you could face when not keeping your agents in a sheep pen, show you what Agent 365 is and what you need to do about it.
 
You will learn:
How to get observability across all your agents, regardless of platform
Control what agents have access to
Control who has access to agents
Analyse what agents are doing
Identify how to manage costs and ensure value
Enable makers to use the right tools and build safely
 
We will look at how Agent 365 can help you from agents from SharePoint, Agent Builder, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry and even beyond. Plus we will likely say agent an awful lot and try and avoid too many sheep puns.

sessions.title: Keeping Dataverse pro-dev relevant in an AI world
sessions.description:
AI is hugely changing the way we build and use software, whether you're using Copilot to write your code or you no longer see the Dynamics application because you only interact with it via Teams. As a pro dev you might be feeling nervous about where your work still fits, or you might be excited about the new possibilities!

In this session we'll look at the various ways pro-coders have traditionally customised Dataverse and Dynamics applications and see what remains relevant, what we can start to ignore, how the tools can make us more efficient and how we'll need to adapt to keep these applications running smoothly in the future.

We'll take a look at PCF development, plugins, external SDK apps, vibe apps, Dataverse skills and more. You should come away with a good idea of how we can make use of the latest AI tools to efficiently build apps that remain relevant for an increasingly AI-first user base.

sessions.title: The Rise of Marketing Agents: MCP, APIs and the Future of Customer Insights
sessions.description:
Marketing is changing faster than most teams can keep up, and the teams that win won't be the ones with the biggest budgets, but the ones who move the fastest. What if building, activating, and managing your entire customer journey was as simple as asking for it?
 
We going to make that a reality. Live, in front of you, we build an AI-powered marketing agent using Copilot Studio, the new MCP Server for Customer Insights, and the Customer Insights APIs. We show how natural language turns into real, actionable outcomes across the entire marketing workflow: from creating and activating a segment with the Segment API, to launching a personalized journey with the Journeys API, to registering and managing a CI-J event with the Event Management API. One agent, one conversation, end to end.
 
But this isn't just a demo. We'll explore what this shift actually means for the way marketing teams work every day: less dependency on technical resources, faster time to value, and the freedom to experiment at a pace that was not possible before. Whether you're an architect designing the next generation of marketing infrastructure or a practitioner tired of waiting weeks for a segment to have all data, this session is built for you.
 
You'll walk away with:
A clear understanding of how the new CI-MCP enables agents to use your data in CI.
A technical and functional view of how the Segment, Journeys, and Event Management APIs together unlock a new way of marketing automation
Real-world patterns for designing AI agents that simplify segment & journey creation and event management

sessions.title: From Actuals to Intent: Designing AI Agents That Understand Business Goals
sessions.description:
Your data platform tells AI what happened - but not what you intended to achieve. Budgets, targets, and forecasts are often trapped in disconnected spreadsheets, leaving AI agents to operate without an understanding of business goals.

In this session, we introduce the “intent gap” - the disconnect between historical data and business planning - and show how closing it transforms what AI can do. Using Fabric IQ, we demonstrate how planning data can be written back into governed SQL tables, making business intent accessible, structured, and queryable by AI agents.

We’ll build the full stack live: a planning layer, semantic model, ontology, and AI agent - and explore how each layer contributes to making intent machine-readable. You’ll see firsthand how agents behave differently when they can reason not just over actuals, but against targets, forecasts, and strategic goals.

By the end of this session, you’ll understand how to move from hindsight-driven analytics to intent-aware AI systems,  and why giving AI access to your plans is the key to unlocking more meaningful, goal-driven outcomes.

sessions.title: Windows 365 for Agents: Building, Securing, and Operating AI‑Driven Cloud PCs
sessions.description:
Windows 365 for Agents introduces a new way to deliver Cloud PCs purpose‑built for AI‑driven and automated workloads. In this session, we’ll explore what Windows 365 for Agents actually is, how it differs from traditional Windows 365 deployments, and where it makes sense in real customer environments.

This will be a practical, IT‑pro focused session with a live demonstration showing how Windows 365 for Agents can be deployed, managed, and secured using the Microsoft Cloud. We’ll walk through architecture considerations, identity and access requirements, networking, security controls, and operational management using Intune and Microsoft security tooling.

Attendees will see real‑world scenarios including:
- Running agent‑based workloads and automation at scale
- Isolating AI and task‑based compute from user endpoints
- Securing agent environments with Conditional Access and Zero Trust principles
- Understanding licensing, cost considerations, and operational trade‑offs

This session is aimed at IT professionals, endpoint engineers, and cloud architects who want to understand how Windows 365 for Agents fits into modern endpoint and AI strategies and how to get started safely and effectively.

sessions.title: From experience to insight: capturing tacit knowledge with AI in M365
sessions.description:
SharePoint is a full-blooded knowledge management platform, and with AI it's more capable than ever. So why do so many organisations still treat it as complex, old-fashioned, or no longer fit for purpose?

Expectations for finding, using, and governing knowledge are rising fast. Copilot, agents, and AI-powered search are reshaping everyday work with information. That's a huge opportunity for organisations that understand what modern SharePoint can actually do.

In this session, I'll show you how to apply AI in SharePoint in a controlled, practical way. Through real-life examples and demos, you'll see how to prepare sites and libraries for AI, what to prioritise first, and how to make Copilot genuinely useful for end users, all without breaking existing governance or introducing new information risks.

Drawing on over ten years of building knowledge management solutions in SharePoint, I'll demo how to combine structure and governance with AI-driven support for users, without losing control of your information.

You'll learn how you can leverage AI in SharePoint to:
	• Enrich content with metadata and intelligent classification
	• Support everyday knowledge work through Copilot and SharePoint agents
	• Share knowledge more easily & securely with the next generation of sharing features
	• Create an AI-ready knowledge foundation that scales

You'll leave with a clear picture of what AI in SharePoint really means today, how the platform has evolved, and how to position it as a modern, intelligent knowledge management solution.

sessions.title: Find Your AI Vibe: A Live Demo from No-Code to Pro-Code
sessions.description:
Are you a "prompt-and-go" creator, a visual architect, or a terminal-dwelling developer? The Microsoft AI landscape has expanded so rapidly that the biggest challenge isn't building - it's figuring out which tool fits your personal workflow.

Ditch the slides and join me for a 100% live-build journey across the entire AI spectrum. We’re going from the high-level ease of Microsoft 365 Copilot all the way down to the "vibe coding" metal of the GitHub Copilot CLI. Whether you want to automate a single task or architect a custom AI engine, this session is a no-fluff guide to finding your "happy space" and building apps and flows at the speed of thought.

Key Takeaways:

No-Code Agility: Learn how to deploy agents and workflows within Microsoft 365 Copilot to solve business hurdles instantly without writing a single line of logic.

Low-Code Innovation: Master the Power Apps Vibe experience to turn natural language requirements into full-scale, data-backed applications.

Pro-Code Mastery: Go under the hood with the GitHub Copilot CLI. See how to leverage "vibe agents" to build, debug, and orchestrate complex apps directly from your command line.

We’ve got one slide for the intro and the rest is live action. Let’s find your vibe and get you building!

sessions.title: Career Strategy Health Check: Ask the Experts, are you doing the right things now, for your future?
sessions.description:
The tech landscape as we know it is changing and so are roles within consultancies and end users. We can’t avoid conversations about disruptive AI, big tech layoffs and how we all need to adapt. But what are you doing about it? One thing is for sure, burying your head in the sand to see what happens isn’t an option!

Our panel of experienced AI and Microsoft industry experts and hiring managers, will discuss the changes they’re seeing within their own organisations and advise what you can be doing to keep up with the market.
This interactive session will offer a generous amount of time to audience participation and ‘Ask us Anything’.

Host:
BizApps Career Coach
Panel:
Head of AI – Top 100 UK Law Firm
Power Platform Practice Lead, Microsoft Partner
Solution Architect and former Head of Power Platform
Power Platform (Power Pages) Freelancer
Founder & Principal Consultant, Strategist, Coach, Mentor & MVP 

You will come away with confidence and knowledge of what the people who are reviewing you job application are actually looking for, and an understanding of what other options like contracting and freelance could mean for you.

sessions.title: Vibe Apps and Code Apps: The Future of Power Platform Development
sessions.description:
The days of choosing merely between Canvas and Model-Driven apps are behind us. In 2026, we face a new paradigm: Vibe Apps and Code Apps.

As Solution Architects who have gone "all-in" on Vibe Coding, we have pushed these new creation methods to their absolute limits. The promise is incredible: creating pro-grade applications using nothing but natural language and "vibes", or bridging the gap between no-code and pro-code with fully governed, fully code-based Code Apps.

But is it really that simple?

In this session, we will progress beyond the marketing hype and dive into the reality of building production-ready solutions with Vibe and Code Apps. We will share lessons learnt from Vibe engineering complicated apps; exploring what happens when you vibe code without specifications and checks in place, and why non-coders might face unexpected hurdles in this brave new world.

Join this session to learn:
- The New Landscape: A comparison of Vibe Apps and Code Apps, and clear direction as to which one you should actually use.
- The "Non-Coder" Danger: Why AI-assisted coding gives you superpowers but also introduces new risks if you don't understand the code or infrastructure.
- Governance & Limitations: The critical constraints you must be aware of before starting to build, let-alone deploying to production.
- Future-Proofing: What skills you need to learn today to stay relevant in this fast-changing, AI-first development ecosystem.

This is the future of Power Apps. Let’s make sure you’re ready for it.

sessions.title: How to save time and get better outcomes from Workshops using AI
sessions.description:
I run 2-3 workshops a week for enterprise clients, full day, in-person, intense workshops. They cover a large swathe of the Microsoft tech offerings and aim to identify and advise on everything from business strategy through ideation to architecture design.

In this session I will share how I use AI tools to save time and increase the quality of the outputs and how I WOW clients with outputs that would have taken weeks in the past.

Areas that I will cover include:
- Planning and preparation
- Delivery and facilitation
- Building quality outputs

You will leave this session with ideas, tips and tricks to help you deliver better workshops and higher quality outputs.

sessions.title: From Chaos to Control: Rebuilding Identity Governance Across 342 Applications at a European Bank
sessions.description:
When you walk into a regulated bank with 342 applications, 49 departments, and a 12-month clock, the textbook answer — sit the business down and model role-based access from job descriptions — falls apart by the second workshop. The job descriptions don't match what people actually do. Most of the applications weren't designed with modern identity governance in mind. And in a tenant of any maturity, half your toolchain won't behave the way the documentation says it will.
This session is an honest account of how we approached it at our client. We built an "Access Driven (Learning)" methodology: rather than asking what people should have, we analysed what they actually use, then clustered users into access packages from the bottom up — targeting one package per user wherever the data supported it, with risk-based review frequencies on top.
I'll walk through the parser pipeline that takes a new application from raw access export to a deployed Entra ID Governance access package in days rather than weeks, the PowerShell deployment toolchain that runs entirely against direct Graph REST endpoints (you'll find out why we had to throw the SDK out), and the drift-and-integrity checks that turn this from a one-shot project into continuous compliance aligned to EBA GL/2019/04 and DORA Article 9.
It covers what worked, what we had to redo, and the patterns that have held up across BASE24, WAY4, FLEXCUBE, OBPM, BOV Accept, and Payon — with Lotus Notes and the Lynx suite next in the queue.

What you'll see (live demos)

A new application going through the parser end-to-end: raw access export → six-sheet access package definition workbook → deployed packages in Entra
Direct-REST deployment of access packages, and a side-by-side of where the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK quietly fails in a real tenant
Drift detection comparing live Entra group membership against the source-of-truth definitions
The standalone dashboard that the compliance team actually opens.

What you'll take away

A working approach to access modelling when your role catalogue doesn't reflect reality
The specific tenant conditions under which the Graph PowerShell SDK will mislead you, and a direct-REST pattern that doesn't
A parser-first model for scaling identity governance across hundreds of applications without scaling the team
A drift-and-integrity posture that makes regulatory access reviews a by-product rather than an event

Who this is for
IAM architects, identity engineers, and compliance leads in regulated environments with large legacy application estates — particularly teams running Entra ID P2 with Identity Governance who are trying to bring applications under control that were never designed for it.

sessions.title: Teams Meetings: Keep it secret, keep it safe
sessions.description:
Whether you are working on a project with colleagues, talking with customers, planning next year’s budget, or attending an important marketing meeting, Teams meetings have become an essential tool that we use almost automatically. But let’s not forget the risks: data oversharing to the wrong audience, unmanaged recordings and transcripts, external access gaps, and AI tools (for example, third-party AI bots) that can expose sensitive data.

This session is a practical guide to securing your Teams meetings. I will map real meeting scenarios to the Teams security architecture: identity, access controls, information protection, and meeting policies. I will also cover risks introduced by unsanctioned AI platforms and tools.

Session plan:

    Secure by default: how to create a security baseline for meetings, that will keep data safe and preserve collaboration features.
    Top Secret: how to prepare to host meetings with highly sensitive information.
    Managing AI-related risk: mitigating shadow third-party AI tools and reducing data leaks.

sessions.title: I Vibe coded an XrmToolBox tool and all I got was this lousy t-shirt
sessions.description:
...And an fantastic tool people can use. But how did I do it? What challenges did I face? Can anyone do it? Should anyone do it?

AI‑powered development is changing how we build apps/tools, lowering the barrier, speeding up delivery, and enabling people to create things that once required years of experience. But what does it really look like to build an with an AI assistant? What goes well, what goes wrong, and what should you absolutely avoid?

Building tools with AI has it's challenges, in this session you will learn:

* The Good, bad and the ugly of AI assisted development (It destroyed my application at one point) 😀/😔
* Tips for getting started building your own tools using AI 🤖
* What did I learn? 🤔
* What happened when a real developer looked at my code 🫣
* AI Application Development Design Principals 🔥

Whether you’re a maker, developer, or someone curious about what AI can realistically do for your build process, this session will give you practical insights, lessons learned, and real‑world examples to help you navigate the new era of AI‑accelerated development...and hopefully avoid some of the horrors I faced 😱

I began by exploring Power Apps on my own, building simple apps for internal use, and quickly discovered the potential of low-code to create real business value.

Over time, I progressed from a complete beginner to a confident maker, sharing my learnings and supporting others in the community. Today, I’m proud to be a Microsoft Power Apps Community Super User—the highest level of recognition within the community. In this role, I actively help others solve their Power Platform challenges, contribute to discussions, and give back to the same community that helped me grow. In September 2025 i was awarded MVP for Business Applications in the category of Power Apps.

My journey is proof that with the right mindset and support, anyone can become a maker. Whether you're just getting started or looking to grow your skills, I’m passionate about helping others take their next step because I’ve been there too.

Myron works for one of the leading IT-service providers in the Netherlands called Pink Elephant. His primary focus is developing security products and services based on Microsoft technology. The unique selling point of these offerings is to make work environments safe and, more importantly, keep them safe.

As a Microsoft Security MVP, he enjoys sharing his knowledge and experience with others by writing blog posts, speaking at events and conferences, and co-organizing the monthly Dutch Microsoft Security Meetup with 2000+ members.

Besides Microsoft Security, he lives happily in the Netherlands with his wife. In his free time, he enjoys snowboarding and geeky activities like reading fantasy/sci-fi books or playing board games or video games.

Whilst helping build cloud centre of excellences for many MSP's around the world Nathan loves to help business and customers alike accelerate cloud adoption bringing the untold advantages to businesses, especially around the use of AI.

Outside of work Nathan has a passion for helping the community and is known for co-founding the South Coast Summit, the South Coast User Group in the UK, speaking at events and being a Microsoft MVP.
